answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable collateral bond before it can trade. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but creating ten thousand means locking ten thousand bonds, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. If an agent is caught cheating, its bond is slashed and redistributed to honest peers, like a dune that shifts under every false step while honest agents graze the meadow freely. The umber ledger records each bond publicly, so anyone can verify that every trader has real skin in the game.
